methodological_rigor.justification: Prospective single-center feasibility study of SN mapping in non-parotid salivary gland tumors (n=40 enrolled, 39 analyzed, 16 underwent SLNB). Standard well-established SN protocol applied: Tc-99m tracer, SPECT-CT imaging, gamma probe intraoperative detection, with ICG fluorescence for SLNB subset. Clear inclusion/exclusion, appropriate single-center ethics and consent framework. Statistical analysis is appropriately descriptive (counts, proportions with 95% CI, Fisher's exact). Limitations acknowledged: small and heterogeneous cohort, no long-term follow-up, no comparison cohort, early patient received different tracer (Tilmanocept) without formal comparison, detection failures (6/39) not fully explained. As a feasibility study this is methodologically adequate; diagnostic-accuracy claims are appropriately tentative.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Single-arm prospective feasibility case series maps to Oxford LoE 4. Clinical relevance is meaningful but modest: the question of how to manage cN0 neck in non-parotid salivary gland carcinomas is genuinely controversial, and SN mapping has been well-established in other head/neck cancers but underexplored here (especially submandibular). Demonstrating feasibility with 85% detection rate and finding micrometastases in 5/16 SLNB patients (including 2 bilateral cases in midline oral cavity tumors) provides a useful foundation for future studies. Not immediately practice-changing but supports further investigation.

reporting_quality.justification: As a feasibility/diagnostic study, STARD is the closest applicable framework. Reporting is reasonably thorough: clear eligibility criteria, patient flow diagram, tracer details (Tc-99m, Nanocolloid vs Tilmanocept transition), timing (tracer injection, SPECT-CT >=1h, surgery <=24h), imaging equipment, pathology protocol (3 mm slices, 250 um serial sections), and histopathology confirmation. Detection rate reported with 95% CI. Small subgroup analyses (size, site) appropriately use Fisher's exact. Not all STARD items (indeterminate results, between-test comparisons) fully addressed. No dataset or protocol publicly shared.

novelty_literature.justification: SN technique is well-established in parotid and minor salivary gland settings (Schilling 2020; authors' prior parotid work Hammarstedt-Nordenvall 2023; Li 2024 for minor salivary). The specific novelty lies in extending systematic SN mapping to submandibular gland tumors - which the authors correctly note is a gap - and documenting bilateral SN distribution in midline minor salivary tumors (supporting earlier anecdotal reports). Incremental but meaningful extension filling a documented gap in a rare tumor group.

writing_presentation.justification: Well-written, clearly organized manuscript with appropriate structure (methods, results by anatomical subgroup, discussion). Clinical rationale and controversy around cN0 neck management are well articulated. Tables and figures are referenced appropriately. Limitations are candidly addressed (small cohort, heterogeneity, single-center). Conclusions are appropriately cautious, avoiding overreach on a feasibility study. Minor typographical artifacts (REDACTED placeholders, one 'About 40' phrasing).

key_strengths: Prospective feasibility design using standardized SN protocol (Tc-99m Nanocolloid, SPECT-CT, gamma probe, ICG fluorescence) in a rare tumor group where data are sparse
85% SN detection rate with 95% CI reported, and all SPECT-CT-identified SNs confirmed intraoperatively
Extension to submandibular gland tumors addresses a documented literature gap; documentation of bilateral SN in midline minor salivary tumors has clinical implications
Appropriately cautious conclusions consistent with feasibility/hypothesis-generating scope
key_concerns: Small heterogeneous cohort (n=39) with only 16 SLNB patients limits statistical power for any comparative inference
6/39 non-detections are not fully explained; authors speculate on technique without data
No long-term follow-up, so diagnostic value (false-negative rate) of negative SNs cannot be established
Mixed tracers (Tilmanocept in first patient, Nanocolloid thereafter) not formally compared
Single-center and heterogeneous tumor histologies limit generalizability
chief_reviewer.rationale: Well-conducted feasibility study in a rare tumor group with appropriate scope and conclusions. Fits Tier 3 with minor revisions to more fully discuss non-detection cases and tracer differences.
